content_units: 9 m² Dublin Kitchen: Best Low-Disruption Upgrade

For a structurally sound apartment kitchen with a   €2,500 budget  ,   minimal disruption  , and a likely sale within   18 months  ,   repainting/refinishing cabinet fronts is the better fit in most cases  . Replacing fronts can look sharper, but it often pushes the budget once measuring, hinge alignment, handles, and installation are included.
Repainting vs Replacing Cabinet Fronts
Option   Typical Cost   Timeline   Disruption   Durability   Resale Impact   Best Fit

Repaint existing fronts     €800–€1,800       2–5 days     Low to medium; some drying/curing time   Good if properly prepped; weaker on chipped laminate/foil   Good cosmetic uplift; strong value-for-money   Best when cabinets are solid and layout is unchanged

Spray-finish existing fronts     €1,200–€2,200       3–7 days     Medium; doors often removed off-site or masked on-site   Better, smoother finish than hand painting   Very good visual upgrade for sale prep   Best if you want a near-factory look without full replacement

Replace doors/fronts only     €1,800–€3,500+       1–3 weeks     Medium; measuring, ordering, fitting   Very good if quality fronts and hinges used   Strongest visual reset, but may not fully pay back before sale   Best if current fronts are damaged, warped, or hard to refinish
Full cabinet replacement     €5,000+       2–6 weeks     High   Highest   Can help resale, but poor fit for your budget/timeline   Not suitable for this scenario
Best match for your priorities
Recommended:     Repaint or spray-finish existing fronts
-   Budget fit:   Most likely to stay within   €2,500
-   Least disruption:   No major carpentry, templating, or long lead times
-   Sale horizon:   Good cosmetic uplift without over-investing before listing
-   Works well because:   Your cabinets are already   structurally sound
Trade-off alternative
Consider replacement of fronts only   if you want a more “new kitchen” look and can accept a tighter budget and longer lead time.
- Better if the current doors are   thermofoil/laminate peeling  , swollen, or badly chipped
- Higher chance of budget creep from   hinges, fillers, panels, handles, and fitting
- Better visual consistency if the old fronts have deep profile styles that still look dated even after painting
What This Means for Cost, Wear, and Saleability
Cost in Dublin context
For a   small 9 m² apartment kitchen  , repainting is usually the most efficient spend. A professional finish may also leave room in the budget for:
- new handles
- soft-close hinge adjustment/replacement
- a fresh splashback paint or minor wall touch-up
- updated lighting
Those small extras often improve buyer perception more than spending the full budget on new fronts alone.
Timeline and disruption
If least disruption matters most:
-   Repainting/spray-finishing   usually wins
- You may lose normal use of the kitchen for only a few days
- Full replacement of fronts often involves   survey, manufacture lead time, delivery, then fitting  , so the project feels longer even if installation itself is quick
Durability
-   Best repaint results   come from proper degreasing, sanding/deglossing, adhesion primer, and a cabinet-grade topcoat
- Painted finishes generally hold up well for normal apartment use, but they are still more vulnerable than factory-made replacement fronts in high-touch areas
- For an   18-month ownership horizon  , repaint durability is often fully adequate if the prep is done properly
Resale impact
For a sale within 18 months, buyers usually respond to:
- clean, bright, modern colour
- neat hardware
- doors closing properly
- no peeling, swelling, or visible wear
That means   a good repaint often delivers most of the resale benefit   at a lower cost. Full front replacement only makes more sense if the existing door material is visibly failing.
Warning Signs That Make Repainting a Bad Idea
If you see several of these, skip repainting and price up   replacement fronts   instead:
-   Peeling vinyl/thermofoil   on MDF doors
-   Swollen or blown edges  , especially near sink/kettle/dishwasher zones
-   Water-damaged MDF   that feels soft or puffy
-   Warped doors   or fronts that no longer sit flat
-   Deep chips, cracks, or broken corners
-   Grease saturation   that keeps bleeding through old finishes
-   Laminate delamination   or loose surface layers
-   Hinge screw holes stripped out   repeatedly
-   Mismatched previous repairs   leaving uneven surfaces that will show through paint
- A door style so dated that colour change alone will not modernize it
A practical rule: if the problem is mostly   surface appearance  , repainting is viable; if the problem is   material failure or distortion  , replace the fronts.
Best Decision for Your Apartment
Given your priorities, the best-value route is:
1. Professionally repaint or spray-finish the existing fronts
2. Add new handles if current ones look dated
3. Tune hinges and align doors
4. Only replace individual fronts that are swollen or peeling
That approach usually gives the strongest balance of:
-   lowest disruption
-   budget control
-   sale-ready appearance
-   reasonable durability for the next 18 months
